I farm in Quzhou County, so I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the steadiest way for me to use the land well, match the local water and climate conditions, and avoid taking risks at my age. I do not want to gamble on crops with harder management or weaker local selling channels. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I care most about stable emergence, disease resistance, and dependable yield. I will fertilize in a moderate way, not too heavy, because input costs matter and I want the crop to stand well instead of growing overly lush. I will irrigate wheat more times because it needs water at key stages, while maize will get fewer irrigations and mostly follow summer moisture unless the field turns dry. I will manage weeds, insects, and disease with a few planned sprays rather than many extra passes. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it fits my equipment and labor strength better than deeper ploughing every time. My goal this year is not maximum risk-max yield; it is steady production, manageable fieldwork, and reliable grain output from the land I know best.
